approve verb

also approve of, approval, approved

classical

Ov. Ars 2.198–200
Ov. Met. 7.20 (Lewis & Short)

probō, probāre, probāvī, probātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

approve, think well of

To judge good and approve; its other senses are “test” and “prove, show” (see prove).

Other words

  • comprobō, comprobāre, comprobāvī, comprobātum — approve fully, sanction

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 69: laudō vehementissimēque comprobō (Lewis & Short)

    Stronger and more formal: to approve wholeheartedly, or to ratify a decision.

  • approbō, approbāre, approbāvī, approbātum — assent to as good, approve; make acceptable, prove

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 7: meum jūs jūrandum ūnā vōce et cōnsēnsū approbāvit (Lewis & Short); Liv. 7.37 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • quicquid probat illa, probātō; quod dīcet, dīcās; quod negat illa, negēs

    whatever she approves, approve; what she says, say; what she denies, denyOv. Ars 2.198–200

  • istam tuam sententiam laudō vehementissimēque comprobō

    I praise that view of yours and approve it most heartilyCic. Imp. Pomp. 69 (Lewis & Short)

  • meum jūs jūrandum ūnā vōce et cōnsēnsū approbāvit

    (the Roman people) approved my oath with one voice and one mindCic. Pis. 7 (Lewis & Short)

See also praise, agree, allow, prove.
